defect.proposed_fix: Split the rule. Keep only the verified constitutional portions, or add disclosed statute/opinion records proving Title III probable cause, particularity, necessity, minimization, high-level authorization, suppression, Keith, and FISA propositions.

reasons: Katz pinpoints address electronic eavesdropping on a public-phone-booth conversation and reasonable expectation of privacy, not all communication contents at the rule's breadth.
Olmstead treatment supports that Katz overruled Olmstead on the privacy point.
Berger pin-56 supports particularity, but the disclosed pin does not verify the full safeguards claim or the Title III element list.
No text/ directory is present, and the Giordano, Scott, and Keith lake records have no pinpoints or stub holding text from which to verify the statutory and domestic-security propositions.
residual_risks: Some statutory propositions may be legally correct, but they are not verifiable from the disclosed files under the review rules.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Narrow to Katz displaced Olmstead's trespass-only privacy point for electronic eavesdropping that invades a reasonable expectation of privacy, and Berger requires particularity; move Title III/FISA details behind separately supported statutory assertions.
